dataVersion.description: Monotonic schema version for extension-owned settings/KV/cache interpretation. The host commits it only after successful registration.

runtime.description: Execution boundary. New distributable Swift extensions should use webAssembly; native is retained for format-1 compatibility.

executable.description: Manifest-relative path. Absolute paths and '.' or '..' components are invalid.

capabilities.description: Safe WebAssembly v1 values include commands, panels, mcp.tools, settings, services.provide, services.consume, companions.invoke, ui.components, ui.rendering.metal, appearance.provider-icons, appearance.account-icons, appearance.session-identity, appearance.themes, appearance.fonts, host.projects.read, host.sessions.read, host.sessions.runtime.read, host.repositories.read, host.providers.read, host.accounts.presentation.read, host.events, storage.kv, storage.cache, and storage.secrets. appearance.themes and appearance.fonts are data-plane: the host reads the declared documents and font files itself, and the running extension gains no new broker operation from either. companions.invoke addresses only operations declared by the same extension's companion. ui.rendering.metal permits constrained host-owned custom surfaces only; it does not grant Metal objects to the extension process. host.sessions.runtime.read returns only host-attributed process and listening-port rows for an exact session ID; it does not grant process-table access. network.client is reserved for deprecated native compatibility and is rejected for WebAssembly. Unknown values remain inspectable but are rejected by hosts that do not support them.

companions.description: Optional separately signed macOS worker apps. Companions extend a WebAssembly core; they do not replace its settings, commands, panels, hooks, tools, storage, or host-data capability boundary.

themes.description: App-theme documents offered to the host's theme library while the extension is enabled. Requires the appearance.themes capability. Each resource is a package-relative JSON file in the host's app-theme vocabulary (the document Skalman stores for a custom theme); the host reads, validates, and namespaces it (ext.<extension>.<id>) at inspection time, before any extension code runs.

fonts.description: Font files (.otf, .ttf, .ttc) registered process-scoped for Skalman's own chrome while the extension is enabled. Requires the appearance.fonts capability. Family names come from the files themselves; the host parses each file at inspection time and names every family in the install disclosure. Licensing of a bundled font is the package author's responsibility.

bundlePath.description: Package-relative path to a nested app. The host rejects absolute paths, '.', '..', symlink escapes, malformed bundles, and mismatched derived bundle identifiers.

capabilities.description: OS-facing companion authority, independently approved from the WebAssembly core's Skalman host capabilities. SDK v1 values are background.service, process.spawn, network.client, network.listen, filesystem.user-selected.read, filesystem.user-selected.write, screen.capture, input.control, automation.apple-events, notifications.post, clipboard.read, clipboard.write, and ui.remote-surfaces.

operations.description: Named, schema-described operations the WebAssembly core may invoke through Skalman's host broker. Declaring any operation requires the core capability companions.invoke.

surfaces.description: Bounded pixel surfaces rendered by this companion into host-owned views. Declaring any surface requires the companion capability ui.remote-surfaces.

accessibilityLabel.description: Host-owned accessibility fallback for the pixel surface.
